fix: Maintainer 2026-11-13: prices x1 at every preset (the point of a fast preset is to get sooner what x1 has): delete the scale or set it to 1, and check what an NPC pays for items stays consistent; rebuild the bot tables
why: the old text mixed the model's money (x1 prices) with the game's x10 table and carried the NPC C gear question, since refuted (C4 NPCs sell up to D)

head: DT-458
what: Economy model: the rule 'a main takes at most one route that needs a fare in a visit' is written twice, in the visit and in payableKit of the attainable measure → the two can drift and the measure then reads a kit no visit could buy
fix: Let the one buy decision (plan-buy2 S2) own the hop rule and the measure call it.

head: DT-459
what: Economy model: the attainable measure spends the money of the last visit but reads today's lines and prices in that town, and leaves out the account wallet the pool kept back → a line posted after the main left reads as a buy-rule gap, one sold since hides a gap; size not measured
fix: Count the readings whose pick changes with the book the main saw at its visit before the buy decision is sized on the measure.

head: DT-460
what: Economy model: payableKit's crystal take (own units first, then the cheapest lines at or under the cap) repeats the visit's take of the same units → the two can drift and the measure then reads a kit no visit could buy
fix: Fold the crystal take into the one buy decision with the hop rule (DT-458).

head: DT-461
what: Economy model: D shot coverage fell from 95.5 % to 94.0 % (levels 30-39: 81.1 to 78.9 %) as better-armed mains raised D shot demand by 45 % (wanted 13.4M to 19.5M in a 40 h x10 run) → D-grade hunters run without shots more often
fix: Size D shot supply (crafters' lines, NPC) against armed demand in the shot-supply work.

head: DT-462
what: Economy model: the per-crystal ceiling of a Luxury route has no test at the place it is weighed: set to Infinity, no test fails → the model could pay ten times the weighed crystal price unseen
fix: Let the design test harness buy crystals from another account's lines and pin the ceiling there.

head: DT-463
what: Economy model: two Luxury exchanges at one visit both count the own twin's crystals → the second exchange is priced as if it still had them
fix: Take the own crystals already claimed at this visit off the count before the next exchange.

head: DT-464
what: Economy model: a main without a spot row takes the game's ranked spot in today and design views but its line's richest spot in plain mode or with no ranker → two answers to one question; plain-mode runs read adena per exp 12-21 % high for those mains
fix: Pass the ranker into plain mode's view and keep the richest spot only as the no-ranker test fixture's answer, or delete plain mode's spot path.

head: DT-465
what: Economy model: the ranked state carries no lifelong kills or own samples, so every rank uses the largest income belief error → 3 of 193 late spot-less picks differ from the save's kills, 89 of 193 at the floor error; ranked mains pick more randomly than the game's experienced bots
fix: Pass the save's lifelong kills and the run's kills into the ranked state.

head: DT-466
what: Economy model: a ranked main re-decides its spot only when the spot is outleveled; the game also re-decides at a grade change, a death and a disappointing spot → over long design runs ranked mains hold spots longer than the game's bots
fix: Raise the earning-spot situations the model can see (grade change, death) as re-decisions when design runs are calibrated.

head: DT-467
what: With honest hunting shares D shot demand in hours 10-20 is 2.4 times what holders craft (wanted 4.49M, crafted 2.29M in a 40 h x10 model run) while 92 % of holders' MP is unused: half the holders' empty wakes find no D crystal (no D crystal route in the crafter's town) → D-grade hunters run without shots for most of hours 10-20 (coverage 26 %)
fix: Size D shot supply: where holders stand against the D crystal route, or crystals reaching holders by lines, against armed demand (DT-461).

head: DT-468
what: After the first sell-outs D shot lines resume a step back and stand above the worth of most shooters in hours 20-30 (2.97M of 4.20M unfired D units sampled above worth; 2.88M crafted units unfired) → level 30-39 hunters fire D shots for 16 % of their hours while shelves hold stock
fix: Measure the step-down speed of a crafter's unsold line against a C4 seller's behaviour and decide whether it overshoots.

head: DT-472
origin: econ track plan-market-knowledge; maintainer 2026-11-13: trade chat by region, prior knowledge not full
what: A bot's price belief reads the first ask and bid on the whole board and its choice of a market town reads every shop town's lines from wherever it stands → bots know every town's market without going there, which no C4 player could
fix: Scope a bot's trade knowledge to its map region plus what it saw on its own visits, by the pure rule the economy model settles first.

head: DT-473
what: Economy model: payableKit and the visit each keep their own count of the twin's crystals and line units already taken around crystalsStanding → a later change to one leaves the kit the path weighs and the kit the visit buys disagreeing
fix: Move the count of own and line units taken so far into one helper beside crystalsStanding, called by both.

head: DT-474
what: Economy model: a claim on a twin's own stock is applied with no check and the goods closure skips stock that is not above zero → an overclaim shows only as a closure failure with no account, item or hour, so each one costs a traced rerun to find
fix: Count every own-stock claim that would take a twin's stock below zero and trace the first one (account, item, units, held, hour) in the run's stats.

head: DT-476
what: luxuryCrystallizes false zeroes the crystals of the 38 Luxury item ids from every source, not only the pieces Luxury sold: a dropped or bid-bought Flamberge or Composite Armor crystallizes to 0 C in design mode → C crystal supply, the input of every Luxury exchange under C AND D, loses those pieces (size not measured; c7base: 53 C crystals in 40 h)
fix: state the reading as 'these items never crystallize' or zero only pieces obtained by exchange; count C crystals lost to it in a run

head: DT-477
what: Economy model: the snapshot carries the Luxury catalogue twice (luxuryOptions from NpcExchangeShopLists + spawns, luxury from data/Bots/hunt/sources.json) → a row changed in one source moves the design's routes and not the item set, unseen
fix: one field (npcId, town, crystals) feeds the routes, the item set and the print; check today mode output unchanged

head: DT-478
what: Economy model, hunt at the worn kit (h2): a D shot line stands over the cap of waiting 40-51 mains for 567 of 726 waiting hours out of shots (base 25 of 187) → 305k D shots unfired (26 % of the loss); not known whether the mains' worth or the twins' asks moved
fix: Count caps against the standing asks per band before any price or worth change.

head: DT-479
what: Economy model: a main that cannot pay the gatekeeper fare there and back waits out of shots while a seller stands in a trade town → 137k D shots unfired in h2 (109k base), 30-39 mostly; a C4 player walks there
fix: Treat a trade town the main cannot pay the fare to as a walk (hours), not as no seller.

head: DT-481
what: Economy model design mode: deathArrival reads the reference kit's deaths an hour (row.deaths) while the hunt reads the worn kit → an under-dressed main dies at a dressed main's rate in the model
fix: Read deaths through the worn kit's hour (kit-hours deathHours) by the same factor path.

head: DT-482
what: Economy model: the static cap/floor report prices a line's own hour and horizon at the reference kit's row, not the entering kit → the report's cap>=floor shares overstate what a main entering the grade earns
fix: Price the report's ownHour and horizon at the entry kit's kill factor (Worth.huntFactors).

head: DT-483
what: Economy model today mode: the hunt reads the reference row for every main and its fit folds the save's mean kit effect into each band's share → per-main kit spread is lost in today runs (kept on purpose so the compare against real runs stays comparable)
fix: Give today mode the same kill factor in hunt and fit together once its compare gate can be re-baselined.

head: DT-485
what: Economy model: the worn and the reference kit's shares come from each kit's own best-net cell, which can be different spots, so the factor divides kill shares measured at two spots → the factor drifts from the main's own spot's ratio by an unmeasured amount
fix: Measure how often the two cells differ, and if it matters take the reference share at the worn hour's cell.

head: DT-486
what: Economy model: two exported functions are named wornKit with different meanings (Mains: kit with the weapon put in its slot; Worth: paperdoll conflicts resolved) → a reader or a later change can call the wrong one
fix: Rename Mains.wornKit to kitInHand (or similar).

head: DT-488
what: Economy model: situations and levers today's code holds outside the registry of rules/levers.js (occupation SITUATIONS, the crafter's wakes and its own-main / sold-since craft levers, the run's CAUSES list) have SPEC rows marked planned or none → the old layer's copies are not tracked for deletion, so a rebuilt row can land beside its old copy unnoticed
fix: mark each as old with a registry pointer when its row is next touched, or delete it in the slice that builds its row

head: DT-490
what: Economy model: when the stacks a visit keeps (worn pieces, shots) fill the bag, bag_full is due at once after the visit → once a trip costs hunting time the main walks back to town after every visit and hunts 0 hours (seen with a 2-slot fixture bag; not reached with 80 slots)
fix: count toward bag_full only what a visit can empty

head: DT-492
what: Economy model: a main low on shots that cannot pay its seller is asked again only at its next other event (level-up, bag_full, goal_affordable, death) → with none it hunts without shots to the end of the run although its money may cover the shots long before
fix: name the hour its money covers the shots over its low mark as a situation, as goal_affordable does (spec row H.SHOTS: money reaching the shots is the waking event)

head: DT-493
what: Economy model: occupation's move at arrived_town prices the extra walk to a re-chosen spot and the fare to another town's spot, but the engine takes no hours for that walk or hop → moves to another town's spot are free in time, so hunt hours read high for movers
fix: carry the move's walk and hop hours as away or since in the engine, as trips now do

head: DT-494
what: Economy model: the shot town re-read at arrival can differ from the planned one while the away hours stay as planned → a hub trip whose seller is gone loses 2 hops for nothing, and a trip planned to the nearest town but sent on to another at arrival gets its hops free
fix: add the re-read town's hop hours at the visit (afterHours) instead of fixing them at the decision

head: DT-495
what: occupation's move at grade_changed, spot_left and recipe_wanted (7,728 of 20,110 moves in t2s1-x10) is neither priced nor timed: the main hunts the new spot at once → hunt hours read high for movers in the field, grade changes cost no trip
fix: make the field move a segment through the same moveHours (from the field: walk back + hop + walk out) handed to the engine, or a grade_changed trip to town (decision layer, after the foundation list)

head: DT-496
what: offerPosted reads shotsLow from since to now across a departed bag_full/goal/death way (shots counted as fired on the way) and counts stats.events.offerPosted although the engine's rearrive is a no-op for a departed main → the offer-posted wake count reads high
fix: count the wake only when the engine asked the rule (rearrive answers whether it asked)

head: DT-497

head: DT-508
what: Economy model: the stamp computation (Boot.dataStamp → TableFingerprint.fingerprint('hunt')) runs while recordReads is on, so its generator-file reads (scripts/hunt-tables/build.js, ceilings.js, corrections.js, rotation.js) enter every later preset's sourceFiles; x10 holds 783 files and x50 787 in one run → the snapshot stamp depends on the --preset order and lists four files that are no input of the snapshot's rows (a change to one already refuses every preset through header.fingerprint, so no run sees it)

head: DT-510

head: DT-511
